name: Exquisite Corpse
description: The surrealists' folded-paper game (also called Consequences), built for a classroom. Six students each add ONE word to a sentence without seeing what came before: adjective, noun, adverb, verb, adjective, noun. Every sentence returns to the student who started it, assembled. Nobody authored it, nobody could have predicted it, and the room finds out together. No points, no winners, no wrong answers.
tagline: Perfect for vocabulary practice, parts of speech, creative writing warm-ups, or pure play.

theme.label: Theme
theme.helper: A nudge for word choices: 'the ocean', 'ancient Rome', 'our vocabulary list'. Leave the default for pure surrealism.

wordTimer.label: Seconds per word
wordTimer.helper: How long each word round stays open. Short keeps the folds moving; 25 is plenty for one word.

template.name: Exquisite Corpse
template.description: A blind pass-and-write sentence built with the Exquisite Corpse recipe, six hands and nobody saw the whole thing coming.

intro.message:
EXQUISITE CORPSE

The surrealists' folded-paper game. We build sentences together, but here's the fold: each of you adds ONE word without seeing any of the words before yours.

Six words, six hands. At the end, the sentence you started comes back to you, finished by five classmates. Nobody knows what any sentence says yet. Not even the people writing it.

word-1.prompt:
Word 1 of 6. Write one ADJECTIVE, a describing word (sleepy, ancient, sparkling, suspicious).

Theme: ${theme}

unfold.message:
Pencils down. Every paper unfolds at once.

The sentence each of you started is about to come back, finished by five classmates who never saw it. Read yours quietly first. Then we'll hear some out loud.

end.message: Six hands, no plan, and somehow it's poetry. The surrealists would be proud.
